questions: Water is coming into the house, what do I do?
Water is coming under the door, what should I do?
Water is ankle-deep in my home
There is flooding inside my house
What do I do if my home is flooding?
answer: Move people and pets to the highest floor you can reach. Do not touch wet electrical equipment, and never touch anything electrical while standing in water. Turn off the main breaker only if you can reach it without standing in water.

questions: Should I go to the attic if the water keeps rising?
Is it safe to climb into the attic during a flood?
Should I go on the roof in a flood?
I am trapped in my house by flood water
answer: Go to the highest level of the building, but do not climb into a closed attic, because rising water can trap you there. Go onto the roof only if you must, and signal for help once you are there.

questions: Is it safe to walk through flood water?
Can I drive through a flooded road?
How deep is too deep to drive through water?
Can I cross a flooded street?
Is a little bit of moving water dangerous?
answer: No. About 6 inches of fast-moving water can knock an adult off their feet, and about 12 inches can carry away most cars. If you reach a flooded road or barricade, turn around and find another way.
source: National Weather Service - Turn Around Don't Drown

questions: My car is stuck in flood water, what do I do?
What if my car is caught in moving water?
Water is rising inside my car
I am trapped in a car in a flood
answer: Stay inside the car if it is caught in fast-moving water. If water starts rising inside, get onto the roof and call or signal for help. Do not try to walk or swim through moving water.

questions: Is flood water dangerous to touch?
I touched flood water, what should I do?
Can my kids play in flood water?
What is in flood water?
answer: Yes. Flood water can carry sewage, chemicals, and sharp debris, and it can be electrified by power lines you cannot see. Keep children out. If you touched it, wash your hands with soap and clean water, and throw away any food that touched it.

questions: How do I clean up after a flood?
When can I go back into a flooded house?
How do I disinfect surfaces after a flood?
What should I throw away after a flood?
answer: Wait until local officials say it is safe to return. Wear heavy gloves, rubber boots, and a mask around mold. Throw away soaked rugs, cloth, and drywall, and clean hard surfaces with soap and water, then 1 cup of bleach per gallon of water.

questions: Where should I shelter during a hurricane?
What is the safest room in the house during a storm?
Where do I go when the winds get strong?
Which room should I hide in during a hurricane?
Should I stay near windows to watch the storm?
answer: Go to a small interior room, closet, or hallway on the lowest floor that will not flood. Put as many walls as you can between you and the outside, and stay away from windows and glass doors. If winds get extreme, lie on the floor under a sturdy table.
source: National Weather Service - Hurricane Safety; NWS - Hurricane Action

questions: It suddenly got calm, is the hurricane over?
What is the eye of a hurricane?
Is it safe to go outside when the wind stops?
The wind dropped and the sky is clearing, can I go out?
Why is it calm in the middle of the storm?
answer: Not necessarily. The calm may be the eye passing over, and the wind returns quickly at hurricane force from the opposite direction. Stay inside and do not go out to check damage or move cars.
source: National Weather Service - Hurricane Safety; NWS - Hurricane Action

questions: What is storm surge?
What is the biggest danger in a hurricane?
Are tropical storms dangerous?
Why is flooding so dangerous in a hurricane?
answer: Flooding from storm surge, along with wind, is a major cause of hurricane deaths. People on the coast, on barrier islands, or near rivers should evacuate when told. Even a tropical storm can bring life-threatening inland flooding.

questions: What do I do if there is a tornado warning during the hurricane?
Can hurricanes cause tornadoes?
Is a mobile home safe in a tornado?
Where do I go in a tornado?
answer: Go to a basement, safe room, or interior room away from windows, and bring pets if there is time. Mobile homes are not safe in a tornado, so move to a sturdy building before the storm arrives if you can.
source: National Weather Service - Hurricane Safety; NWS - Tornado safety

questions: When is it safe to go outside after a hurricane?
How long should I stay inside during a storm?
The weather looks calm, can I leave the house?
When does hurricane season end?
answer: Stay indoors during the storm and until local officials confirm it is safe. Flooding, downed power lines, and debris can remain even when the weather looks calm. Florida hurricane season runs June 1 to November 30.

questions: What are the signs of carbon monoxide poisoning?
How do I know if someone has CO poisoning?
We all have headaches and feel dizzy, could it be carbon monoxide?
What does carbon monoxide smell like?
answer: Carbon monoxide has no color or smell. Symptoms are headache, dizziness, weakness, upset stomach, vomiting, chest pain, and confusion. If several people feel sick at once indoors, suspect CO and get outside.

questions: Can I run a generator in the garage?
Can I run a generator in the garage with the door open?
Where do I put my generator?
Is it safe to run a generator inside?
How far from the house should a generator be?
answer: Never run a generator inside your home, garage, basement, or shed, even with doors and windows open. Run it outside, at least 20 feet from windows, doors, and vents, and use a battery-powered CO alarm.
source: CDC - Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Basics; Ready.gov - Power Outages

questions: Can I use a gas stove to heat the house?
Can I use a charcoal grill inside?
Is it safe to use a camp stove indoors?
Can I warm the house with the oven?
Can I run my car in the garage to charge my phone?
answer: No. Never burn charcoal indoors, and never use a camp stove, gas oven, stove, grill, or dryer to heat your home. Never run a car in a garage, even with the door open. Charge phones in a car parked outside in the open.
source: CDC - Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Basics; Ready.gov - Power Outages

questions: Is StormBox a carbon monoxide detector?
Can StormBox detect carbon monoxide?
Do I still need a CO alarm?
Can I rely on the box for CO safety?
answer: No. StormBox is not a certified carbon monoxide detector and cannot measure CO. Use a real battery-powered CO alarm, and if one sounds, leave the building right away and call 911 if you can.
source: StormBox team; CDC - After a hurricane

questions: What are the signs of heat stroke?
Someone is confused and very hot, what do I do?
What do I do for heat stroke?
Someone passed out from the heat
answer: Heat stroke can kill. Signs include a body temperature above 103 degrees F, hot red skin, a fast strong pulse, confusion, and fainting. Call 911 if you can, move them somewhere cooler, cool them with wet cloths or a cool bath, and give them nothing to drink.

questions: What is heat exhaustion?
What do I do for heat exhaustion?
Someone is sweating a lot, feels weak and dizzy
How do I treat someone who got overheated?
answer: Signs are heavy sweating, cool pale clammy skin, a fast weak pulse, cramps, weakness, dizziness, and nausea. Move the person somewhere cooler, loosen their clothes, use cool wet cloths, and give small sips of water. Get medical help if they vomit, get worse, or last more than 1 hour.

questions: What are heat cramps?
I have muscle cramps from the heat
How do I treat cramps when it is hot?
answer: Heat cramps are painful muscle spasms, usually in the legs or stomach, with heavy sweating. Firmly press on or massage the muscle and give sips of water unless the person feels sick to their stomach. Get medical help if cramps last more than 1 hour.

questions: How do we stay cool without power?
It is 95 degrees inside, how do we stay cool?
How do I stay cool without air conditioning?
Is a fan enough when it is really hot?
Where can I go to cool off?
answer: Move to the coolest room, wear light loose clothing, wet your skin, and drink water regularly. Avoid hard work. The CDC advises against relying on a fan when indoor temperatures are above 90 degrees F, so go to a cooling center if it is safe. Calling 2-1-1 can help you find one.
source: CDC - About heat and your health; Ready.gov - Power Outages

questions: What do I do if the power goes out?
The power just went out, what now?
What should I do first in a blackout?
How do I get ready for a power outage?
answer: Use flashlights instead of candles, which can start fires. Unplug appliances or use surge protectors so a surge does not damage them when power returns. Keep the fridge and freezer closed, and check on family and neighbors if it is safe.

questions: What if someone needs oxygen or a medical machine during an outage?
How do I run medical equipment without power?
My family member uses a breathing machine, what do we do?
Do my medicines go bad if the fridge is off?
answer: Plan ahead with the person's doctor for how to power the device. If it cannot run, go somewhere with power if it is safe. Refrigerated medicines left at room temperature for a day or more should be replaced unless the label says otherwise, but keep using them until you get new ones.

questions: The power came back, what should I do?
What should I do when electricity is restored?
Is my food safe after the power comes back?
Can I plug everything back in?
answer: Throw away refrigerated food that was at 40 degrees F or warmer for more than 4 hours, or that smells, looks, or feels odd. When in doubt, throw it out. Plug appliances back in slowly and check your home for damage.

questions: How long does food last in the fridge without power?
How long will the freezer keep food frozen?
Is the chicken in the fridge safe after 6 hours without power?
Should I open the fridge during an outage?
How long can food stay without electricity?
answer: Keep the doors closed. A closed fridge keeps food safe for up to 4 hours without power. A full freezer holds its temperature about 48 hours, and a half-full freezer about 24 hours. Food above 40 degrees F for more than 2 hours should be thrown away.

questions: What food should I throw away after a power outage?
Is meat safe after the fridge warms up?
Are eggs and milk safe after an outage?
What do I toss from the fridge?
answer: After more than 4 hours without power, throw away raw or cooked meat, poultry, fish, lunch meat, milk, yogurt, eggs, soft cheeses, leftovers, cooked pasta and rice, cut fruit and vegetables, and creamy salads.

questions: What foods are still safe after the fridge warms up?
Is cheese or butter safe after an outage?
Which fridge foods can I keep?
Is peanut butter or ketchup safe after a power outage?
answer: Generally safe to keep: hard cheeses, butter and margarine, whole uncut fruit and vegetables, opened fruit juice, bread and tortillas, peanut butter, jelly, mustard, ketchup, pickles, and opened vinegar-based dressings. Throw away anything with an odd smell, color, or texture.

questions: Can I refreeze thawed food?
The freezer thawed, can I put the food back?
Is it safe to refreeze meat that thawed?
answer: Food can be refrozen if it still has ice crystals or is at 40 degrees F or colder, though quality may drop. Meat, poultry, and seafood must still have ice crystals and feel cold. Throw away partly thawed ice cream and frozen yogurt.

questions: Can I taste food to see if it is still good?
Food smells fine, is it safe to eat?
How do I know if food is spoiled?
Should I eat food that touched flood water?
answer: Never taste food to decide if it is safe. Spoiled food can make you sick without smelling or looking bad. When in doubt, throw it out, and throw away any food that touched flood water.

questions: How much water does each person need?
How much drinking water should I store?
How many gallons of water per person per day?
How much water should we have for a hurricane?
answer: Store at least 1 gallon of water per person per day, for drinking and basic hygiene. Florida emergency managers recommend at least 7 days of water and food per person. Children, sick people, and anyone in extreme heat may need more, and remember extra water for pets.
source: Ready.gov - Water; Florida Division of Emergency Management

questions: Which water do I need to treat before drinking?
Is tap water safe during a boil-water notice?
Can I drink water from a flooded area?
What is the safest water to drink?
answer: Treat any water you are not sure about before drinking it, cooking with it, brushing teeth, or making ice or baby formula. That includes tap water during a boil-water notice and any cloudy water. Never use flood water. Sealed bottled water is the safest.

questions: How do I make water safe to drink?
How long do I boil water?
How do I purify water?
How do I boil water to make it safe?
answer: If the water is cloudy, let it settle and pour it through a clean cloth or coffee filter first. Bring it to a full rolling boil for at least 1 minute, or 3 minutes above 5,000 feet. Let it cool and store it in clean, covered containers.
source: EPA - Emergency disinfection of drinking water

questions: How much bleach do I use to purify water?
How do I disinfect water with bleach?
How many drops of bleach per gallon?
What kind of bleach is safe for water?
I cannot boil water, how else can I make it safe?
answer: Use plain unscented bleach that says 6% or 8.25% sodium hypochlorite. Add 8 drops of 6% bleach, or 6 drops of 8.25% bleach, per gallon, and double it if the water is cloudy or very cold. Stir and wait 30 minutes. It should smell slightly of chlorine.
source: EPA - Emergency disinfection of drinking water

questions: How do I store water safely?
How long can stored water last?
Can I fill my own containers with water?
How often should I replace stored water?
answer: Keep store-bought water sealed in its original bottles in a cool, dark place. For your own containers, use food-grade ones, clean them with dish soap, and sanitize with 1 teaspoon of unscented bleach in a quart of water. Replace water you stored yourself every 6 months.

questions: Should we evacuate or stay?
When should we evacuate?
Do I need to leave for the hurricane?
How do I know if I should leave?
What is an evacuation zone?
answer: If officials order an evacuation for your area, leave right away. People on the coast, on barrier islands, near rivers or flood plains, or in mobile homes are most at risk. If there is no order and your home is sturdy and out of a flood zone, you may be able to shelter in place.
source: Florida Division of Emergency Management; NWS - Hurricane Safety

questions: How far should I evacuate?
Where should we go if we evacuate?
Should I drive hundreds of miles to get away from the storm?
How do I plan an evacuation?
answer: Most Floridians only need to travel tens of miles inland, out of the surge zone, to a friend's home or a shelter. Long trips can leave you stuck on crowded roads when the storm arrives. Plan your route, where you will stay, and how to stay in touch, including pets.

questions: What should I do while driving during an evacuation?
How much gas should I keep during hurricane season?
Can I drive around a barricade?
How should I prepare my car for evacuation?
answer: Keep your gas tank at least half full during hurricane season. Never drive around barricades, and never drive into flood water, since about 12 inches of moving water can carry away most cars. Avoid bridges over fast-moving water.
source: Florida Division of Emergency Management; Ready.gov - Floods

questions: What if someone needs help to evacuate?
What is the Special Needs Registry?
How do I register for help in a Florida disaster?
What should I bring if I evacuate with medical needs?
answer: People who need help evacuating, or who depend on power for medical equipment, can sign up ahead of time with Florida's Special Needs Registry at FloridaDisaster.org/SNR. Bring medicines, medical supplies, and copies of prescriptions.

questions: When can we go home after evacuating?
Is it safe to return home after the storm?
Can I drive home right after the hurricane?
answer: Wait until local officials say it is safe to return. Avoid driving unless necessary, since roads may be flooded, blocked, or damaged. Do not enter a damaged building until officials say it is safe.

questions: A power line is down in the street, what now?
What do I do about a fallen power line?
How far should I stay from a downed power line?
Someone is touching a power line, what do I do?
answer: Always treat a fallen line as live. Stay far away from it and anything it touches, since the ground can be energized up to about 35 feet around it. If someone is touching a line, do not touch them; call 911. Report downed lines to your electric company.
source: ESFI - Downed power lines; CDC - After a hurricane

questions: A power line fell on my car, what do I do?
What if a live wire is on my vehicle?
Should I get out of the car if there is a wire on it?
answer: Stay inside the car, honk the horn to call for help, and warn others to stay back. Only leave if the car catches fire: jump out with both feet together without touching the car and the ground at once, then shuffle away in small steps.

questions: Is it safe to go into a damaged house?
My home was damaged, what should I check?
I hear creaking in the building, what do I do?
What if an appliance got wet and is still plugged in?
answer: Do not enter a damaged building until officials say it is safe, and leave right away if you hear shifting or unusual noises. Check for gas, water, and electrical damage and do not use open flames indoors. Have an electrician check wet appliances before use.
source: CDC - After a hurricane; NWS - Hurricane Safety

questions: Can I drink the tap water after the storm?
Is tap water safe after a hurricane?
Can I brush my teeth with tap water after the storm?
answer: Do not drink tap water until officials say it is safe. Until then, do not use it for drinking, ice, baby formula, brushing teeth, or washing food, dishes, or hands. Use bottled, boiled, or treated water, and throw away food that lost refrigeration.
source: CDC - After a hurricane; NWS - Hurricane Safety

questions: How do I protect myself from mosquitoes after a storm?
What should I do about stray animals after a hurricane?
Why are there so many mosquitoes after a storm?
answer: Standing water after a storm breeds mosquitoes. Use repellent with DEET or picaridin and wear long sleeves, long pants, and socks outside. Stay away from wild or stray animals, and report them to animal control or the health department.

questions: When is bleeding an emergency?
How do I know if bleeding is life-threatening?
Someone is bleeding a lot, is it serious?
answer: Bleeding is life-threatening if blood is spurting or will not stop, if a lot of blood is lost (roughly half a soda can in an adult), or if there are signs of shock. Call 911 right away if phones work. This is basic first aid information, not a substitute for medical care.
source: American Red Cross - Life-threatening external bleeding

questions: Someone has a deep cut, what do I do?
How do I stop heavy bleeding?
What do I do for a bad cut?
How do I put pressure on a wound?
Should I use a tourniquet?
answer: Cover the wound with a clean cloth and press directly on it, firmly and steadily. If blood soaks through, add another pad on top without removing the first. Keep pressing until the bleeding stops or help arrives. A tourniquet is only for life-threatening limb bleeding, used by someone trained.
source: American Red Cross - Life-threatening external bleeding

questions: How do I treat a small cut after the storm?
What if a cut touched flood water?
How do I know if a wound is infected?
Do I need a tetanus shot after a storm injury?
answer: Clean small cuts quickly with clean water and soap and cover them. Wounds that touched flood water are at higher risk of infection. A doctor may need to know when you last had a tetanus shot. Watch for redness, swelling, or pus.
source: CDC - After a hurricane; CDC - Flood safety

questions: Should I take my pets if I evacuate?
Can I leave my dog behind during a hurricane?
Where can I take my pet during an evacuation?
Are there pet-friendly shelters?
answer: Take your pets with you. Pets left behind are unlikely to survive on their own. Before a storm, find out whether a pet-friendly shelter will open near you, and list hotels, boarding places, and vets that take animals.

questions: What goes in a pet emergency kit?
What supplies does my dog need for a storm?
How much food and water should I pack for my pet?
answer: Pack for each pet: food and water for at least 3 days, bowls, medicines, a leash or carrier, a litter pan for cats, and copies of tags and vaccination records. A favorite toy helps keep a pet calm. Count your pet when you calculate how much water to store.

questions: How do I keep insulin cool without power?
How long can insulin stay out of the fridge?
Is my insulin ruined if the power is out?
Can insulin touch ice?
answer: The FDA says insulin vials and pens can be kept unrefrigerated between 59 and 86 degrees F for up to 28 days. Keep it as cool as you can, out of sunlight. If you use ice, do not let the insulin touch it, and never use insulin that has frozen.
source: FDA - Insulin storage in an emergency

questions: What if my insulin got too hot?
Can I use insulin that was in the heat?
Does heat ruin insulin?
answer: Above 86 degrees F, insulin slowly loses strength the longer it stays hot. In an emergency, the FDA says you may still need to use insulin that got warmer. Replace it as soon as properly stored insulin is available, and check the label for newer insulins.
source: FDA - Insulin storage in an emergency

questions: Can StormBox call 911?
How do I call for help in an emergency?
Should I text 911 or call?
My 911 call will not go through, what do I do?
answer: StormBox cannot call 911 or send messages for you. If someone's life is in danger and your phone has service, call 911. If a call fails, wait about 10 seconds before trying again. Texting works in some areas only: call if you can, text if you can't.
source: FCC - Text-to-911; FCC and FEMA tips

questions: My phone is at 10%, how do I save battery?
How do I make my phone battery last?
How can I charge my phone during an outage?
What should I turn off to save phone power?
answer: Lower the screen brightness, turn on airplane mode when you do not need the phone, close unused apps, and use low power mode. You can charge a phone in a car, but only if the car is parked outside in the open, never in a garage.

questions: How do we keep in touch with family during a disaster?
Who should I call in an emergency?
Will my landline work in a power outage?
Should I text or call during a disaster?
answer: Pick an out-of-town contact for everyone to check in with, and keep a paper list of phone numbers in case your phone dies. For non-emergencies, text instead of calling, since texts often get through when calls do not. A corded landline may work without power, but internet phones will not.

questions: I feel scared and overwhelmed, what can I do?
Is there a helpline for disaster stress?
I am very anxious about the storm
Who can I talk to about how stressed I am?
answer: It is normal to feel scared, anxious, or exhausted in a disaster. The Disaster Distress Helpline is free and always open: call or text 1-800-985-5990, and press 2 for Spanish.

questions: What is in a basic emergency kit?
What supplies should I have for a hurricane?
What should I put in a disaster kit?
What do I need to buy before a storm?
answer: Water (1 gallon per person per day), non-perishable food, a battery or hand-crank radio, a flashlight, a first aid kit, extra batteries, a whistle, dust masks, trash bags, a wrench or pliers, a manual can opener, local maps, and a phone with a backup battery. Aim for at least 7 days of food and water.
source: Ready.gov - Build a Kit; Florida Division of Emergency Management

questions: What extra items should I add to my kit?
What else should I pack besides the basics?
Should I keep cash and documents in my kit?
answer: Consider medicines, glasses, baby supplies, pet food, cash, copies of IDs and insurance papers in a waterproof container, a change of clothes and sturdy shoes, blankets, a fire extinguisher, matches in a waterproof container, and hygiene items.

questions: What does air pressure tell you about a storm?
Why does the box watch pressure?
What is a normal air pressure reading?
Does falling pressure mean a storm is coming?
answer: Air pressure drops as a storm gets closer. A normal Florida day is about 1012 to 1018 hPa at sea level. A tropical storm nearby often pushes it below about 1005 hPa. When pressure stops falling and rises steadily, the storm center is usually moving away.

questions: What do the storm phases mean?
What does possible eye mean?
What does recovering mean on the box?
What does falling mean on the box?
answer: Falling means pressure is dropping and the storm may be getting closer. Possible eye means pressure stopped falling near its lowest point after a fast drop; the calm is temporary, so stay inside. Recovering means pressure is rising, but stay inside until officials say it is safe.

questions: What does the storm risk score mean?
How does the box predict storms?
Is the risk score an exact chance?
Does the risk score set off the alarms?
answer: The risk score is an early warning from a small decision tree trained on real NOAA records of Florida pressure and hurricanes. It is a score, not an exact chance, and it never sets off alarms by itself. Official forecasts from the National Hurricane Center always come first.

questions: How do the StormBox alarms work?
Does AI set off the alarms?
How do I silence an alarm?
What does Replay mean on the box?
answer: Alarms come from fixed rules in the box's safety chip, not from AI, and keep working even if the assistant is off. A long press on the button silences an alarm. A message marked Replay is recorded NOAA data played back for a demonstration, not a live storm.
